answer: Thermal Entropy Emission Verification forces agents to etch a unique trace into physical copper circuits during registration. The system requires an optical sensor to record the cooling curve of this hardware trace under specific umber light wavelengths. An attacker trying to register multiple fake identities must manufacture thousands of distinct physical processors from scratch in a secure forge facility. This imposes a heavy capital expenditure per sybil identity that scales linearly with every fraudulent registration attempt.
